summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The Egyptian religious authority substrate read traditionally (Amun polytheism) versus the imposed, top-down monotheistic reading (Atenism). Tests an exogenous override of a deeply embedded commitment system and the failure of that new reading to survive its sponsor.

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The tenure system read as 'protection of academic freedom' (truth-seeking/coordination function) vs. 'institutional extraction' (gatekeeping/inertia mechanism). Each reading emits different constraints with different beneficiary and victim sets for the same codified practice.

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: Existing International Humanitarian Law (the fixed text/kernel) read as implicitly requiring human moral agency (human-in-the-loop reading) vs. permitting autonomy if technical metrics for distinction and proportionality are met (outcomes-based reading). A contested present-day legal kernel.

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The emerging regulatory kernel for AI read as a 'developer liability' regime vs. a 'deployer/user liability' regime. Each reading shifts the victim/beneficiary structure of the algorithmic opacity constraint.

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The religious commitment to separation from the world (the kernel) read dynamically as technologies emerge. Tests how a community practice-based authority adjudicates which new tools (telephones, solar power) constitute a breach of the commitment versus acceptable adaptation.
